solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Renovator, one angling to get round former pope (one off)

indicators.note: getting round something means going about it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: someone who angles is a fisher

indicators.note: 'off' says the named item is taken away, as a button comes off a coat

parts.note: Urban was the name of several popes of the past
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A home improver who also fishes gets around an old pontiff, with an aside in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(one off)' reads like an aside but is an instruction on the pope's name: 'one' as the article an is the part that comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbisher polishes up or restores things, so the word is a fair synonym for someone who renovates.

clue.text: Form of amnesia, forgetting eastern edible fish

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so a letter drops away from the word

parts.note: a fugue is a state of memory loss in which a person wanders from home
E is the standard abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone loses their memory and forgets which oriental fish is safe to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: FUGUE drops its E to give FUGU.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugu is the Japanese puffer fish, eaten as a delicacy despite its poison when badly prepared.

clue.text: Sinuous tart took the initiative, getting one flustered

indicators.note: something sinuous twists and winds, so the letters are bent out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, ready for rearranging
to take the initiative is to lead, past tense led

explanation.surface: A slinky seductress makes the first move and leaves her target in a fluster.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rattled is to be unsettled or agitated, the same state as being flustered.

clue.text: Value support

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reference value from which others are reckoned
second meaning: the foundation or stand on which something rests

explanation.walkthrough: Two bare nouns read like a phrase about financial backing; each is a separate meaning of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a starting figure for calculation and the bottom part that holds something up.

clue.text: Long-running serial and accordingly a mishmash

parts.note: so means therefore, accordingly
taken as written
pie is printers' type jumbled together, hence any mishmash

explanation.surface: A complaint that a never-ending TV drama has become a confused muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE (also spelt pi) is jumbled printing type, a classic crossword word for a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapie is Australian slang for a soap opera, the typical serial that runs for years.

clue.text: Well-informed about part of photonovel (5, two words)

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word is wanted, a run of its letters

parts.note: letters two to six of the word

explanation.surface: Someone knows all about one section of a story told in photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hot on a subject is the idiom for knowing it thoroughly.

clue.text: Constituent of ipecac to note for throwing up in the evening

indicators.note: in a down clue throwing something up turns it to read from bottom to top
'in' places the turned word inside the one that follows

parts.note: ene is an old variant of even, the evening
item as an old verb means to set down in a list, to make a note of

explanation.surface: Advice to take a note of an emetic to make yourself sick at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For throwing up' looks like part of a description of an emetic, but it is the turning signal. Ene is an old variant of even, meaning evening, as in Hallowe'en.
explanation.definitionFit: Emetine is the alkaloid extracted from ipecacuanha root that makes the drug induce vomiting.

clue.text: Masked image, thing with end obscured

indicators.note: when the end is hidden from view the final letter is not seen

parts.note: matter is a thing, substance or affair

explanation.surface: Describing a photograph partly covered, its far end blacked out.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER loses its last letter. In film, a matte is a mask that blocks part of a shot so another image can be combined with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A matte is a film image made using a mask, so it is literally a masked image.

clue.text: Dwarf was famously one stout errant, working?

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tubby wandering dwarf at work, as in Snow White's mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Sneezy, one of Disney's seven dwarfs, who were famous for working in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sternutator is something that causes sneezing, or one who sneezes, which is Sneezy's whole character.

clue.text: An Italian vehicle, one with pains once getting doubled up inside

indicators.note: the turned letters are put inside the word for a vehicle

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: doubling up bends something back on itself, and in a down clue the letters run upward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
tene is an archaic word for grief or pain

explanation.surface: An Italian in a van bent double with pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubled up' suggests someone writhing in pain, but in a down entry it sends the letters upward. 'Once' marks the pain word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian comes from Venice, so the word names one kind of Italian.

clue.text: Frolic before number one marriage — Scotch drunk

parts.note: a caper is a playful skip or frolic
No. is the abbreviation for number
I is the Roman numeral one
marriage ties two people together, the knot

explanation.surface: A wild wedding party where the Scotch whisky has gone down well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' seems to be the whisky, but it labels the answer as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Capernoitie is a Scots word for muddled or tipsy, so it means drunk in Scotland.

clue.text: Chum maybe slugs round in repetitive performance

indicators.note: 'in' puts the turned word inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: rote is mechanical repetition

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so it reads backwards

parts.note: slugs are bullets, ammunition

explanation.surface: A friend keeps throwing punches over and over in a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slugs' looks like blows or garden pests; here it means bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: A roommate shares your room and is often a friend, so a chum is an example, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: It may catch you speeding round after bachelor party's over?

indicators.note: when something is over it is turned over, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: a stag party is the British name for a bachelor party
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Driving home too fast after a stag night is likely to get you caught.
explanation.walkthrough: A Gatso is a type of roadside speed camera common in Britain, named after its Dutch maker; a stag party is the groom's night out before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gatso is a speed camera, a device that photographs drivers who break the speed limit.

clue.text: Jock's bound to take tour away from his taxman

indicators.note: taking a part means removing it, the first half of the instruction
taking something away from a word leaves the rest behind

parts.note: a stentour is a Scots assessor of taxes, from stent, a tax
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is determined to keep the tax inspector from going on his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock' is a nickname for a Scotsman, so 'Jock's' marks Scots words; 'his taxman' is a Scots word too. STENTOUR minus TOUR leaves STEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sten is a Scots word for a leap or spring, a synonym of bound.

clue.text: What corrupt emporium conceals presto

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the word tucked away within its letters

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A shady shop hides something that vanishes in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presto' looks like a conjuror's word for something appearing; here it is the musical direction meaning fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptempo means played at a fast speed, as presto directs a musician to play quickly.

clue.text: Volume of added liquid robbing cordyline of energy finally

indicators.note: robbing takes something away, so a letter is removed from the plant name

parts.note: the ti tree is a cordyline, the cabbage tree of New Zealand
E is the symbol for energy; here it is the last one in the word

explanation.surface: Someone drains energy from a pot plant by pouring in a measure of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: TI-TREE loses its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: In a titration the titre is the measured volume of solution added to reach the end point.

clue.text: Ecstasy and LSD distributed rarely in the past

indicators.note: things that are distributed are spread around, so the letters end up in new places

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recreational drugs were seldom handed out in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Seld is an archaic word for seldom, so it means rarely in older English.

clue.text: With which one views from afar endlessly frisky gypsy girl

definitions.text: With which one views from afar

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped
frisky letters jump about playfully into a fresh order

parts.note: the word with its last letter lost
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A lively gypsy girl is watched from a distance through a telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small telescope, the instrument for looking at distant things.

clue.text: Old means of defence, one chaps installed in pile?

indicators.note: what is installed in something is fitted inside it

parts.note: a pile of money is a mint
I is the Roman numeral one
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A castle defended by one man and his chaps installed in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile' suggests a castle or stately building, but it is a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniment is an obsolete form of muniment, which once meant a defence or fortification.

clue.text: Part of bone enters rump after it's minced

indicators.note: mincing chops something up so its letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A butcher's note: bone goes into rump steak once it has been minced.
explanation.definitionFit: The presternum is the front portion of the breastbone, the sternum.

clue.text: Hawk seen from below perched on ancient seat

indicators.note: viewed from beneath, a down entry is read upward, back to front

parts.note: perched means sat
sell is an archaic word for a seat or saddle

explanation.surface: A bird of prey glimpsed from beneath, roosting on an old chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen from below' sounds like a birdwatcher's view; in a down entry it means reading upward. 'On' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Tassell is an old spelling of tassel or tercel, the male hawk.

clue.text: Leading musicians, such as merit's rendered abnormal

indicators.note: rendered abnormal means made irregular, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the letters of 'as merit', the possessive s not counted

explanation.surface: Top musicians, whose excellence is made extraordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, an eminent conductor or musician.

clue.text: Dental gaps at aforementioned back, trapping chewed meat

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside
going back means the letters run the other way
chewed food is broken up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: said, as in 'the said person', means aforementioned
taken as written, ready for rearranging
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gaps in the teeth trap bits of chewed meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' applies to both the short word and 'aforementioned' together, and the turned pair then traps the chewed meat between its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Diastemata is the plural of diastema, a space between teeth.

clue.text: Youngsters with yen for mini

parts.note: teens are teenagers
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Teenagers with Japanese money buying miniskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two pieces; 'mini' is an adjective here, not the skirt or car.
explanation.definitionFit: Teensy is a colloquial word for very small, just as mini means tiny.

clue.text: One driving oxen gets road all snarled up

indicators.note: something snarled up is tangled, so the letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cattle drover finds the road completely jammed.
explanation.definitionFit: A goadster wields a goad, the pointed stick used to drive oxen.

clue.text: Sense of hopelessness at getting lost in analysis

indicators.note: what gets lost inside something disappears from it

parts.note: anatomy can mean a detailed analysis, as in the anatomy of a crisis
taken as written

explanation.surface: Despair at becoming lost during therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Analysis' suggests psychotherapy, which suits the despair; it is ANATOMY, which loses AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomy, or anomie, is a state of alienation and purposelessness, a loss of values and hope.

clue.text: Endless deception brought about Dido's end? Typical of Aeneas

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter is lost
bringing something about wraps it round another piece

parts.note: a deception is a trick, here without its final letter

indicators.note: 'end' keeps only the last letter of 'Dido'

parts.note: the last letter of Dido

explanation.surface: Aeneas's endless deceit brought about the death of Dido, who killed herself when he left her.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIC goes around O. In Virgil, Dido, queen of Carthage, killed herself when the Trojan Aeneas deserted her.
explanation.definitionFit: Troic means Trojan, and Aeneas was the Trojan hero, so something Troic is characteristic of him.

clue.text: Girl displaying cotton twill

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a hard-wearing twilled cotton cloth

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a girl showing off her denim, but the girl's name and the fabric are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is both a female forename and the strong twilled cotton fabric from which jeans take their name.

clue.text: Wild cat said to appear where coastal drives occur

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A wildcat is reported to be seen beside a seaside road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drives' look like motoring, but they are long golf shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Links are seaside golf courses, where golfers hit drives near the coast.

clue.text: Collations like those consumed without footwear by travellers

indicators.note: consumed by something means swallowed up inside it

parts.note: sales reps are commercial travellers
as means like

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
hose are stockings or socks

explanation.surface: Meals such as those eaten barefoot by travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed' looks like eating, which suits meals, but it means swallowed up inside the travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A collation is a light meal and a repast is a meal, so the plurals match.

clue.text: Without gravity, mature over a long time in space

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to mature is to age
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
on means over, as in 'on top of'

explanation.surface: Weightless, a body ripens over ages in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE plus ON loses its G.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immense age; in astronomy it is a billion years, a span used for cosmic time.

clue.text: Meals? With each ignored I contrived to lose weight

indicators.note: contrived means artificially devised, so the letters are arranged anew
what is ignored is left out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
ea. is the abbreviation for each
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter skipped meals as a contrivance to shed pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: MEALS minus EA leaves MLS, which with I is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To slim is to diet and become thinner, the same as losing weight.

clue.text: Crowning this king involves pink toga

indicators.note: to involve is to entangle or coil up, so the letters are twisted together

parts.note: the letters taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coronation ceremony requires the monarch to wear a pink toga.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer together with KING is a jumble of PINK TOGA, so taking KING from those letters leaves the answer to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of, which is what a crown is to the head, so crowning works as a synonym.

clue.text: Developer's constituent, one plenty backed

parts.note: me is what one calls oneself

indicators.note: something backed is moved backwards, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: a lot means plenty

explanation.surface: A property developer has one plot, and plenty of financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developer' suggests a builder, but it is the chemical used to develop photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Metol is a chemical used in photographic developing solutions.

clue.text: Expert in herbal medicine has cut troublemaker on register

parts.note: has cut short is the contraction 's, as in he's
an imp is a mischievous troublemaker
a register is a list

explanation.surface: A herbalist has struck a rogue off the official register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like removal from the register; it only shortens 'has' to 's.
explanation.definitionFit: A simplist is someone versed in simples, the old name for medicinal herbs.

clue.text: Soft coral that's supplanted centre of calcium compound

indicators.note: a compound is formed by combining, so the letters are mixed together
to supplant is to replace, so one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill

indicators.note: 'centre of' keeps only the first letter of 'calcium'

parts.note: the middle letter of calcium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea creature in which a chemical has taken the place of calcium.
explanation.walkthrough: YON replaces the central C of CALCIUM to give CALYONIUM, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcyonium is a genus of soft corals, such as dead man's fingers.
